newsitem.title: UK: BT extends rebound, helped by $1bn bond issue.
newsitem.headline: BT extends rebound, helped by $1bn bond issue.

text.p: British Telecom Plc rose in active trade early on Wednesday, extending a bounce from last week's two-month low and boosted by Tuesday's $1 billion bond issue, dealers and analysts said.
"BT came off last week and there was a buyer around this morning," said one market-maker in the stock. BT shares were up 4-1/2p, or one percent, at 436 by 0751 GMT in volume of 2.1 million shares.
Analysts said the stock continued to be underpinned by hopes for BT's planned merger with MCI Communications Corp as well as prospects for a special dividend to be paid out as part of the merger.

SBC Warburg yesterday repeated a "buy" rating on BT on the back of the company's 30 million stg investment in telesales, which the brokerage said would give greater capability to sell a range of new services and support BT's core business.

Mike Stiles, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, pointed out that BT plans a presentation later this month on new technology developments including its "video-on-demand" service which could also be encouraging interest in the stock.
Stiles added that yesterday's bond issue had been well received in the debt market, which had also helped sentiment in BT shares.
